C.answer: Crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in large document collections by being provided with a description of the document cluster's topic along with propositions. They were not shown the documents themselves, but instead were asked to score each proposition's importance using a 5-point Likert-scale. This approach allowed them to determine important elements without requiring them to read all documents in a cluster.

B.reason: Explains topic description, individual propositions and 5-point importance scoring without reading all documents; supplied text supports each claim.
B.answer: Crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in large document collections by being provided with a description of the document cluster's topic along with individual propositions. They were asked to score each proposition's importance using a 5-point Likert-scale, without needing to read all the documents in the cluster. This approach, called low-context importance annotation, allowed them to efficiently determine important elements by focusing on single propositions rather than entire documents.
